project.title: Proteomic analysis of Lineage negative bone marrow cells from wild-type and Dcaf8 knockout mice
project.projectDescription: To explore the mechanisms by which DCAF8 deficiency induces functional defects in hematopoietic stem cells with an aging-like phenotype, and given DCAF8’s role as a substrate receptor in the E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, we conducted proteomic analysis on Lineage negative bone marrow cells from wild-type and Dcaf8 knockout mice. This analysis aimed to identify protein alterations, providing insights into potential substrates of DCAF8 in murine hematopoietic cells.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Bone marrow cells were collected and lineage positive fractions were depleted. Cell pellets were lysed with 2% SDS containing 50nM DTT, followed by alkylation with 200 mM iodoacetamide and protein precipitation using pre-cooled acetone overnight. Trypsin digestion was performed overnight at a 1:50 trypsin-to-protein ratio. The resulting peptides were then eluted using C18 Ziptips, dried using a SpeedVac (ThermoSavant) and reconstituted in 10 μl of 5% acetonitrile with 1% formic acid. Analysis was performed on a Thermo Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an Easy-nLC 1200 system (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were separated on a 15 cm long, 75 μm inner diameter column packed with 2 μm reverse-phase resin (PepMap RSLC) using a 60-minute gradient from 95% solvent A (0.1% formic acid, 2% acetonitrile, 98% water) to 28% solvent B (0.1% formic acid, 80% acetonitrile) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min. The mass spectrometer operated in positive ion mode with data-dependent acquisition, performing a high-resolution full scan from 350 to 1500 m/z, followed by fragmentation of the top 20 multiply charged ions (excluding single-charge and unassigned ions) at 30% collision energy.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were analyzed using PEAKS (version 10) software (Bioinformatics Solutions) for de novo sequencing and database searching against the UniProt human proteome database (March, 2020). Mass tolerances were set at 10 ppm for precursors and 0.02 Da for fragments. Semi-specific cleavage allowed two missed cleavages. Carbamidomethylation of cysteine was specified as a fixed modification, while methionine oxidation and N-terminal acetylation were variable. FDR was adjusted to < 1%.
